name: Identity Provider Support-Session Theft
description: Lapsus$-style scenario: an attacker compromises a session at the IdP's third-party support contractor and uses the support console to view (and partially impersonate) corporate users. Suspicious password resets and admin actions hit the corp tenancy from the IdP's own infrastructure.
reasoning: Identity provider tenancy is the affected service. Anomalous admin actions originate from the IdP's own back-end IPs, not the corp admin laptops — that's the tell.

nodes.label: okta-support-tier-egress
nodes.notes: Okta's own support contractor source IPs.

narrative.text: Quiet baseline. Support sessions average ~2 admin reads per day.
Anomalous burst: 11 'View user as' actions from support egress IPs in 6 minutes.
Three of those users have password reset triggered + new MFA factor enrolled.
UEBA flags: 'admin actions from support tier on production tenancy spiked 8x baseline'.
Corp security pages IdP vendor; gets confirmation of a contractor-account compromise.
All sessions opened in the last 72h forcefully revoked across the entire corp tenancy.
Support-tier access from vendor temporarily disabled until vendor's investigation closes.
Re-enabled with stricter just-in-time access + corp-side approval for any 'view as'.

okta.note: support tier acting on user accounts
